ety.text: Literally, "to make one's own owl straight".

Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *आडु (āḍu, “peach”), a wanderwort of unknown origin. See there for more. Cognate with Classical Persian آلُو (ālū), whence Hindi आलू (ālū). Also cognate within Indo-Aryan with Punjabi ਆੜੂ (āṛū) and Sindhi آڙو (āṛo).
Learned borrowing from Sanskrit आर्यावर्त (āryāvarta, “Aryavarta”, literally “land of the Aryans”). Compare Persian ایرانویج (ērānwēj).
From उत्तर (uttar, “northern”) + काशी (kāśī, “Kashi, a name for Varanasi”), literally “Varanasi of the North”.

Hindi verb set खेलना (khelnā) खिलाना (khilānā) खिलवाना (khilvānā) Inherited from Prakrit खेलइ (khelaï, “to play”), 𑀔𑁂𑀮𑀡 n (khelaṇa, “playing”), of uncertain further origin. See there for more. Cognate with Nepali खेल्नु (khelnu), Marathi खेळणे (kheḷṇe), Konkani खेळ्चे (kheḷce), Bengali খেলা (khela), and Assamese খেলা (khela). Related to Romani khelel, Sinhalese කෙළිනවා (keḷinawā, “to play”), and Sanskrit खेलति (khelati).

Derived from Sanskrit जम्भ (jámbha) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀟- (-ḍa-) + -𑀓- (-ka-), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ámbʰas, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵómbʰos. Doublet of जंभ (jambh). Cognate with Marathi जबडा (jabḍā).
Compare Sanskrit धक्कयति (dhakkayati, “to annihilate, destroy”). Probably from धक्का (dhakkā, “shove, push”).
